transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex R., Priya S., Marta L., James K., Lena O., Tom E.

Auto-summary: Customer exploring model choice and deployment path. Wants high-accuracy multilingual generation, long-document context for contracts and call transcripts, and ability to call internal tools (search, calendar). Concerned about latency and cost for 128k context windows.

----
00:00 Alex Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Alex at Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone today?
00:10 Marta Lopez: good, thanks. we've been looking at a few options, mostly hosted APIs but may need private. wanted to pick your brains.
00:18 Priya Shah: great, super. can you give a quick picture of workload? do you expect single-turn chat, long document ingestion, or retrieval-heavy flows?
00:28 Marta Lopez: it's mostly retrieval + summarization of legal contracts and multi-ling customer support transcripts, so long context. sometimes multi-ling — english/spanish/portuguese and occasional french.
00:40 James Kwan: infra side, we're leaning toward VPC/private deployment for sensitive docs, but cost and ops are a concern.
00:50 Alex Rivera: totally. Redwood can do hosted for fastest time to value, dedicated reserved GPU pools for steady throughput, and private VPC/on-prem for full isolation. each has tradeoffs on latency/cost and control.
01:05 Tom Earle: from security we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration — we run AWS KMS — and full audit logs, retention controls. does Redwood support that in private?
01:20 Priya Shah: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS and expanded audit logs, and our dedicated offering has strong isolation too; hosted API offers encrypted-at-rest and in-transit, plus SOC2 for the managed plane. we'll send the SOC2 report.
01:36 Marta Lopez: ok good. let's talk models — we evaluated Llama 3, Mistral, and some newer open weights. latency and cost are big, but accuracy on legal text is critical.
01:50 Priya Shah: when you say legal text, are you trying to generate, summarize, extract entities, or all of the above?
01:56 Marta Lopez: all of the above; extraction + structured output is important for our downstream pipelines. we'll need tool-calling to run a named-entity extractor and to hit internal search.
02:08 Alex Rivera: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs. our runtime can stream tokens and call out to tools with a defined schema; we also support retrieval augmented generation pipelines with prefix caching so repeated doc hits are cheaper.
02:25 James Kwan: about context length — some contracts run to 100k tokens once OCR'd. do you have recommendations for 128k windows? what's the cost delta?
02:36 Priya Shah: so practically for 128k you have two patterns. one is chunk + retrieval where you index and retrieve nearby chunks; cheaper and works well. second is full-context window models that keep entire doc in memory — higher cost and latency. we have model profiles tuned for 8k/32k/128k. quantized 8-bit kernels help, but 128k often needs more memory and GPU time.
02:58 Marta Lopez: hmm okay, we prefer full context for certain workflows (legal review) to preserve cross-reference. can Redwood Dedicated handle that?
03:10 Priya Shah: yes, Dedicated can be sized to handle large kv cache and long sequences; we can set up reserved capacity with burst to handle peaks. Private on-prem gives you the most headroom but requires more ops.
03:22 Tom Earle: latency — if we go full-context 128k, what's typical tail latency?
03:28 Priya Shah: depends on model size. smaller quantized models with 128k windows might be in the few seconds per response; for 7-13B class models optimized kernels we see 2-5s for a long summarize, but 70-100B unquantized can be 10s+. We'll run a benchmark against your sample docs to be precise.
03:50 Marta Lopez: and accuracy — are there open models that do legal extraction well? We've seen Llama 3 fine with some instruction tuning, Mistral seems strong on reasoning, and some labs' models have legal-fine-tuned versions.
04:05 Alex Rivera: yes, we curate model catalog and recommend a mix: apply smaller optimized models for high-throughput routes and route critical, high-cost queries to bigger models. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model combos per route.
04:18 Lena Ortiz: multilingual is key — Spanish/Portuguese — do you have evals for these languages?
04:23 Priya Shah: we run multilingual eval suites; some open models drop off in Portuguese. we can run a quick eval with your sample prompts to show per-language accuracy.
04:33 James Kwan: tool-calling specifics — we want the model to call our search API and an internal named-entity extraction microservice behind auth. how does the auth flow look?
04:43 Priya Shah: we support signed short-lived tokens for tool invocation and can integrate with your SSO. For hosted, we'd broker calls or you can host tool endpoints in a VPC peering setup in private deployments. We'll detail patterns in the security pack.
04:57 Tom Earle: does Redwood log outbound tool calls? we need to audit who invoked what.
05:03 Alex Rivera: yes, audit trail includes token-level traces, tool invocations, and per-request headers — retention configurable in private/dedicated.
05:12 Marta Lopez: any hard limits on concurrent requests for dedicated? we expect bursts at end of month for contract processing.
05:20 Priya Shah: dedicated supports autoscaling policies and configurable burst capacity; we'd size pools and add buffer for monthly peaks.
05:28 Marta Lopez: great. what about fallback policies? if a model is overloaded do you gracefully send to a smaller model?
05:33 Alex Rivera: yes, smart routing lets you define fallbacks — route to cheaper model or queued path. you can set latency SLOs and fallback thresholds.
05:41 Lena Ortiz: pricing — is there a simple per-token cost for 128k? or it's more complex?
05:47 Alex Rivera: pricing varies by model and deployment. for hosted it's per-token plus model multiplier; dedicated is committed capacity with a unit cost; private is licensing + infra. We'll send a sample pricing for 8k/32k/128k profiles.
06:00 James Kwan: for the benchmark can you include hosted vs dedicated and show 95th percentile latency and cost per 1k tokens?
06:08 Priya Shah: yes, we'll include P95, throughput, and token cost. also recommend one or two model variants per latency tier.
06:15 Marta Lopez: on compliance, we need to know about data residency — we have EU customers. can private be deployed in EU region?
06:22 Alex Rivera: yes, private deployment can be in customer region; dedicated and hosted have region options and data residency controls. We'll list supported regions in the security doc.
06:33 Tom Earle: one more, do you integrate with our AWS KMS for key rotation?
06:37 Priya Shah: yes, customer-managed KMS with rotation is supported in private/dedicated, hosted has managed KMS with customer key options for higher tiers.
06:45 Marta Lopez: ok, that helps. walk me through a recommended pilot — what would Redwood do in a 6-week pilot?
06:53 Alex Rivera: typical pilot: week 1 gather sample prompts and infra details, week 2 spin up hosted/dedicated benchmarks, week 3 run multilingual/accuracy evals, week 4 iterate on model/config, week 5 integrate tool-calling and retrieval connectors, week 6 run final acceptance tests and handoff.
07:16 Marta Lopez: timeline is tight — we'd like pilot started by mid-March.
07:20 Alex Rivera: we can aim for kickoff 2026-03-18 as discussed.
07:24 James Kwan: ok, action items?
07:27 Alex Rivera: I'll send security pack and pricing by Friday, Priya will configure a benchmark plan; James will share network and KMS info.
07:35 Marta Lopez: perfect. thanks.

Questions noted:
- Will Redwood provide sample quantized models for low-cost inference? (Answer: yes, we can provide quantized variants and recommendations)
- Can tool-calling be audited at request-level? (Answer: yes, audit logs capture tool calls)

Reference links mentioned: security pack (link to shared drive), benchmark template (link to spreadsheet), product deck (link to redwood deck) — participants agreed Alexis will share links after call.

End transcript.
